utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. The Chamber understands there are one or two matters that counsel wish to raise. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Very briefly, before the next witness enters the courtroom, I'd simply like to provide two more pieces of information related to this witness, in case the Chamber deems it necessary to discuss these matters with the witness. The Chamber is aware, I believe, as is the Defence, that the Prosecution has had discussions with the witness over the last few days about his "suspect status" and the implications thereof. And I would like to simply point out two facts from the last -- from these discussions. The witness inquired at one point whether the affirmation provided to the witness by the Prosecution, yesterday afternoon, would also -- would protect the witness from subsequent prosecutions in his home country or in other countries. And the Prosecution has explained to the witness twice in the last few days that the -- that the Office of the Prosecutor's affirmation declaration cannot provide such a sweeping guarantee, if you will, for the future. However, the Prosecution also has explained to the witness the text of Rule 90(E), about the witness's right not to incriminate himself; and if he is compelled to answer certain questions, that the Chamber can determine that such evidence would not be used in subsequent prosecutions. And with that explanation, the witness was willing to go forward. The Prosecution also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, in that, I sense an implication that the effect of Rule 90(E) would be binding upon a court of a nation. It's certainly binding on this Tribunal, but why would it bind a court in another country? Would it not depend upon the law of that country, whether evidence given under compulsion was admissible or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I take Your Honour's point. Yes, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour. Also, yesterday -- the witness came to The Hague without an attorney; and during discussions yesterday and further explanation of the meaning of the suspect status here at the ICTY, the witness was also given an opportunity to telephone legal counsel in Macedonia. And the witness declined that opportunity and said, no, he was ready to go forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, once again, that would apply under Rule 42 to questioning by the Prosecutor in your investigation role.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But it has no direct application to evidence given in this court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. It is simply the Prosecution's policy now to continue, if you will, to treat someone who was treated as a suspect during the investigation to continue to permit that person to consult with an attorney, if they so wish. And so that opportunity was given to the witness yesterday. I simply wanted to make that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Is there any other matter? If not, the witness should be brought in. Oh, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise. First of all, I'm grateful to my colleague, Mr. Saxon, for raising the point. We had discussed it with him this morning. So we are grateful that we did so. There's one other matter, very briefly, Your Honour, which we wish to raise this morning, and that concerns the appeal hearing in the Halilovic case which will take place on the 10th and 11th of July of this year. I myself will be involved in this appeal as co-counsel for Mr. Halilovic, and I intended this morning to make an application for a short recess, perhaps, in this trial on the 10th and 11th of July for reasons that I will produce. I will not be able to attend the hearing in both cases at the same time. I have talked to Mr. Saxon this matter about this matter, and he has indicated to me that he would have no objection to this matter. I understand it may create some delays and, perhaps, some problems with this Chamber, but I hope that Your Honour will be minded to grant this application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, the -- in view of the position of the Prosecution, and even though the matter will have, obviously, the effect that two days of hearing might be lost, the circumstances persuade the Chamber that there should not be sitting on the 10th and the 11th of July. If there should be any adjustment to the Appeals Chamber sittings, you could let us know; but at the moment, the Prosecution should plan on the basis that there will be no hearing on the 10th and the 11th. We realise that leaves the 9th as a single day, and we also realise that that may produce problems with bringing a witness and starting evidence and then waiting for two days. So that realisation being identified, we leave it to you, Mr. Saxon, as you come nearer to the 9th, 10th, and 11th, to indicate whether there will be a particular problem about the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the Chamber and to the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I believe we're now ready for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you please read aloud the affirmation that is on the card shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honours, and everyone else present in the courtroom, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Judges understand that you have been formally advised by the Office of the Prosecutor that you will not be charged by this Tribunal with any offences in relation to the events at Ljuboten during August 2001. We mention that in court so that you can be re-assured that that is the position of the Prosecutor announced publicly. This Tribunal cannot direct that there will not be proceedings in your own country or in some other country, but we can assure you as far as this Tribunal is concerned that there will not be any proceedings against you in The Hague. We would further mention to you that if you believe you are asked to speak about a matter that could incriminate you, that is, that could amount to some admission of your guilt of an offence or could provide material evidence that you have committed an offence, then it is open to you to say that you do not wish to answer that question. We understand this has been explained to you by the people from the Office of the Prosecutor that have been speaking to you, but we mention it specifically in court so that you are aware of the matter. So you may indicate during your evidence, if at any time you feel that a question put to you would require you to incriminate yourself in the way that I have indicated. I believe now Ms. Motoike has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. Your Honour, for the record, the Prosecution at this time calls Mitre Despodov.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good morning. Sir, is your name Mitre Despodov?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: In August 2001, were you the major in command of the 3rd Guardist Battalion of the 1st Guardist Brigade for the Army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And up to that date, that is, August 2001, how long had you been in the military?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this: How many years up to August 2001 had you been in the military?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Army of the Republic of Macedonia or combined with my service in the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. With respect to the Army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I was in the Army of the Republic of Macedonia since April 200 ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises: I'm not sure about the year, if the witness could repeat the year.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Despodov, the interpreter didn't here the year. What year did you -- what year did you say you were -- you had begun in the Army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I was in the Army of the Republic of Macedonia since April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. And drawing your attention to August of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, with respect to this witness, because of the exhibits that we intend to tender, I have prepared binders, if we could distribute those with the assistance of the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, drawing your attention to August 2001, I would like to show you, if we could, please, 65 ter 794.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It's at tab 1 of the binders. Its ERN is N001-4698-N001-4698. Thank you. And could we turn it. Thank you. Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, do you see what's being displayed in front of you on the computer screen?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this appears to be a map with some markings on it. Do you recognise this particular map?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And drawing your attention specifically to the right portion of the map, towards the centre, maybe the third grid down, it says "Ljuboten" there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And there appear right above that appear to be some triangles with some numbers in them going from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, I believe. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, what those specific markings, the triangles with the numbers, do those indicate the positions of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia at the time, in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honours, those are the positions of the 3rd Guardist Battalion, of which I was the commander, and the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 denote the points the positions of the 2nd Guardist Staff, which was in my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then right below that, following that train of thought, right below that, there's also some positions marked with triangles. Is that also a location of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Are you referring to the positions in the village of Rastak? "3/3 Guardist Battalion," that writing?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Those are the positions of the 3rd Staff which was deployed at the village of Rastak.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And drawing your attention up to -- above to the left and above Ljuboten, there is a bigger triangle with some handwritten brackets around it. Can you please indicate for us what that is.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will ask you what specific triangle are you referring to? I did not understand well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I apologise. It's my fault. There's a town, I think, marked on here. On the map, it says "Ljubanci." Do you see that? It's right near the "2" with the circle.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And immediately to the left of that is a big triangle with some handwritten markings around it. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us what that triangle indicates.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honours, the triangle in the village of Ljubanci with the flag to the left of it, to the north of it, where "3" is written is the topographic marking for the command location of my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And was your command location located in a specific building within Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours. In the primary school, in the village of Ljubanci, in the building of the dorm. That dorm was intended for orphans or children of impoverished parents who receive social welfare assistance and they stay here, the children from the neighbouring villages, in the Skopska Crna Gora mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Were there two locations for what I'll loosely term has your headquarters for the 3rd Battalion? Was there one in Ljubanci and another in I think you've described being in the hills or in the Skopska Crna Gora mountain? Was there another location there as well?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honours, at the command position of the battalion was located in the village of Ljubanci, as I explained already. While the command location for the 2nd Guardist Company, the unit that was deployed above the village, as I explained before, that was positioned in the dorm. There is -- in the children's resort, there is the children's summer resort next to the St. Ilija church.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. So, if I'm looking at this map correctly, then, is the companies within your battalion, their positions are then located in the upper right area of this map, near the Rastak and Ljubanci/Ljuboten area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: According to the deployment that is depicted here, the 2nd Company up there, above the village of Ljubanci; the third in the village of Rastak; well around Ljuboten, and above Ljuboten we had no positions, no posts.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you also have a 1st Company to your battalion?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: There was another company there, but it is not depicted here in the map. It was to the left of the 2nd Company near the village of Brodec. It is a bit further away from these villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we tender this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P297, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Despodov, thinking -- keeping this map and the locations in mind, I would like to show you another map which is tab 2 of today's binders. It's 65 ter 117. And this map, Mr. Despodov, that you see before you is somewhat colour-coded. A little bit clearer as far as the locations of the villages. Do you see to the left of the map it says "Ljubanci," and then right below that to the right it says "Ljuboten." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And there are some markings, red dots with lines, that kind of -- they're in the centre portion of the map, and they go up from right above Ljuboten and they follow in kind of an upward line to the right of the map. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, again, do those indicate the positions of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia at that time, in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, with their titles, the names we had given them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the names that -- these are the names in the squares above, these red dots, these are the names of the particular companies?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Not of companies. No, I apologise, Your Honour. This is part of a company, a group of five to six reservists who make that position, and they have a title. For instance, the 1st Base, they were named.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And you can see some -- there is a reference to a 3rd Company in the -- it's in English. It's to the right -- right portion of the diagram. So these red dots along the diagram then indicate the position of the army, just so we're clear for the record. Is that true, Mr. Despodov?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And at that time, as the commander, were you familiar with the positions of the National Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Not in detail, Your Honour, based only of -- on the information that I had at the time. They were stationed in the village of Ljuboten, in Strima, Matejce as well. And they were moving up and down the ridge of Crna Gora mountain, from Nikustak, Aracinovo, down the road to so-called Muratovo Djade road. And this is where they were maintaining the connection between the units deployed in Bresta, Matejce, Tanusevci, Strima, and Ljuboten, and inside the city of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention to the left portion of the map, there are some dots that are -- they look like they're red, but I believe they're a lighter colour red and maybe a magenta, to be more specific. And those spots are marked Kuljm, Ecmeniste, Rastanski Bacila, and Matejce. Do those positions sound familiar to you as positions that were occupied or took by the National Liberation Army at the time?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, as a commander, were you also familiar in the area with respect to police positions that had been taken by the Ministry of the Interior at that time?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention then to the light blue markings on the left of the diagram, they indicate Stratiste; ambulance; and Braca house, "Chinese wall." Do those three positions sound familiar to you as the positions that the police had been at the time?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention, lastly, to the middle of the -- upper middle of the diagram, it has a big huge star with many points. Can I ask you first, actually, whether you're familiar with a mine explosion that occurred on 10 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention then to this star with many points in the middle of this map, where it says "Ljubotenski Bacila," is that the location of where that mine explosion took place?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we please tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P298, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, I would like to show you a few more photographs so we could know where the Macedonian army was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we please show the witness N005-7991. With the assistance of the usher, we have a bigger panorama to show. It is tab 3 in today's binder. Could we please put it on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, looking at the photograph, you have the full photograph displayed on the screen; and then to the left of you, with the assistance of the usher, there's an actual hard copy of the photograph there on the ELMO. Do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this is a photograph, actually, of Ljuboten village with the Skopska Crna Gora mountain range in the background. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could you please, if you're able to recall, mark on the hard copy that's on the ELMO, with the assistance of the usher, locations that are at least visible, and that is the locations of the Macedonian Army, that are visible on the photograph. Are you able to do that for us today?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honours, on this photograph, on the right-hand side, the overall area of the village of Ljuboten, I could do that. However, on the left-hand side, I am not too familiar with that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. If you could please mark for us then the positions that you can at least note from the right, I guess, part of the photograph. The hard copy might be easier because it's bigger, if you could do that, please.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: On this photograph, I am not really able to do so. On the right-hand side, where the location of the 3rd Company, however, much away to the right-hand side, and those positions are not really visible on this photograph, either on the hard copy, on the one that I can see in front on the monitor. This is the part on the right-hand side viewing from the mosque. The positions of the 3rd Company were further to the right, and this is not visible on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Are any positions that your battalion had at that time, in August 2001, are any positions visible to you on this map or this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can do that for the 2nd Company on the photograph on the right-hand side, on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If you could, please, do that then. Perhaps using the hard copy, so that we have a bigger scale, could you do that using the hard copy of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes. I can do that, but not the -- currently the part that is presented now, but the photograph on the left-hand side. These are a couple of locations. The other ones are not visible because they are behind this ridge, this hill, and then it goes along the line between the two positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Just for the record, you've marked two red lines on this particular photograph, and those would indicate the positions, then, that are visible on this photograph that were taken by the 2nd Company of your battalion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then slight -- right before -- right as you did that, you also indicated with your finger that there were other positions above this bottom red line on the photograph that you've marked, that go along the mountain range, that are not visible because they're beyond the hills. Would that be accurate?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And are those the only positions then that are visible to you on this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: On this photograph, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P299, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, if I could show you one more photograph, it's located at tab 4 of today's binder. It's 65 ter 199.28.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Actually, the photograph that's displayed is the same one. Could we have 65 ter 199.28. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, in August of 2001, you mentioned the 2nd Company of your battalion. Was that commanded by Captain Mario Djurasic?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honours, not under command of the name of the person you mentioned, but his name is Mario Jurisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry. I mispronounced it. And could we take a look, please, at this photograph that's before you. Do you recognise what's depicted in this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It is a panorama of the village of Ljuboten from the positions somewhere around the position of the 2nd Company, where it was deployed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And so this 2nd Company, again, this would be where the captain was Mario Jurisic?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: His company was deployed there, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And just so that we're clear, is Ljuboten village then just beyond this -- towards the centre of the photograph, just beyond these trees here, downward into that valley that's depicted in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes. The village that is visible is Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And perhaps, just so we're all clear, could you maybe use the Stylus with the assistance of the usher, and mark the area that we're talking about which would indicate the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: The village that is visible down there is the village of Ljuboten. The road here is the so-called Ljuboten road leading to Radisani and Skopje, and the road to the left leads to the village of Rastak.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, so, for the record, you've indicated a road which would lead to Skopje, I believe -- Radisani, which is the line that goes upwards on the right side of this circle that you've indicated, and then you've also indicated a line that goes out of the middle of the circle to the left, which would indicate the road to Rastak. So this circle that you've drawn -- I'm sorry. The photograph then does not depict the entire village of Ljuboten. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: No, just a larger part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P300, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Despodov, with respect to the mine incident that we talked about a little while ago, did you prepare a report with respect to the events that occurred on that particular day, which would be 10 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and it was handwritten and I submitted it to my command.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please show the witness 65 ter 60.2, which is tab 8 of today's binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, there are two documents displayed in front of you; one in English and one in Macedonian. If I could have you look at the upper left corner of the Macedonian, it indicates, "Commander of the 3rd Guardist B, Ljubanci village," and it's dated 10 August 2001. It says it's a report on executed terrorist attack submitted, and then it indicates to the right, "2 VP 2454." And the first photograph, it says: "On 10/8/2001, around 800 hours, the vehicle m/v IVEKO 21102, driven by soldier Simic Dejan from VP 3560/19, living in the village Tromegja (Kumanovo) returning the shift from the position Zdravec, with the rear right wheel ran over an explosive device." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the second page, please, in both documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At the very bottom, Mr. Despodov, of this page, it says: "Commander Major Mitre Despodov," with a signature. Is that your name and signature there?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention to the last paragraph on both pages, it says: "The measures of combat security were strengthened in the entire region of the battalion, and especially monitored is the region of the village of Ljuboten and the village itself, in cooperation with members of MOI," which is Ministry of the Interior, "who arrived in the afternoon hours." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we tender this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P301, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, drawing your attention to this last sentence of this particular document, you indicate that members of the Ministry of Interior arrived in the afternoon hours, which would be 10 August 2001. Could you describe for us or tell us, please, if you can recall, who were these persons who arrived.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honours, in this sentence, I was thinking about a patrol that was used additionally besides the check-point that was located in the village of Ljubanci; however, they stayed for some time and then they left.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Were there other persons who came from the Ministry of Interior on the 10th of August, 2001, to see you?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: In the evening hours, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, who were these persons, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, although in my previous statement, I have provided this information. That evening, at the command post, a representative from the Ministry of Interior arrived who introduced himself with his name; however, to -- even today I cannot remember who the person was and his name. I provided his detail description in my previous statement. Mr. Johan Tarculovski was there; Mr. Ljube, the commander of the police station in Butel or Cair, I believe; and Mr. Slavco, the commander of the police station in Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And did you know Johan Tarculovski at that time, when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: That was the first time I've met him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Did you know where Mr. Tarculovski worked at that time?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: He introduced himself, and he told me that he's in the personal security of the president, Boris Trajkovski, now deceased.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: For the person whose name you cannot remember at this time, can you please tell us -- do you recall what that person's occupation was?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I couldn't, really, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Did this person tell you, this person that you can't recall whose name it was, did this person tell you -- well, let me ask you this: Did this person say anything to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. He told me that the police undertakes an operation in order to take over the village of Ljuboten, and he came to inform himself whether I, through my superiors, along the command line have received orders or instructions or precise tasks in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can we go back a second and you've described -- you said it was -- they came to see you at the command post. Would that be the command post that you've described to us as being at Ljubanci, at the school?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And did Mr. Tarculovski tell you anything at that time, during that meeting with him?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: During this meeting, Your Honour, Mr. Tarculovski was acting nervous because he could not understand that somebody somewhere along the line of distribution of orders and tasks can -- can fail or he did not believe the lack of responsibility of certain officers at certain levels.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall specifically what these persons asked of you at the time when you met them?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: This person that I explained earlier, that I cannot remember - and I really don't remember his name - he just wanted to know that whether I received some kind of order or task written in relation to that forthcoming action.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the person you said -- you've described as Ljube and the other person as Slavco, did they indicate anything to you at that time during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I got the impression that they only showed them the road. They brought the people, the people that I mentioned earlier, to the command post in order -- in order to show them around. Throughout the meeting, they did not say anything in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall what these persons were wearing at the time of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage or terrain field police uniforms with the insignia of the police of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And what did you say in response to their inquiries?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just informed them that I still have not received any order, task, written or orally, by my command post, and I didn't know what was all about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall what Mr. Tarculovski's response was, if anything, was to this -- your statement to them?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: It -- he was a bit undecent with lack of culture; however, this is understandable in such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, did he say anything to you with respect to your response and that you did not receive an order?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Literally?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: He told me, if I remember it well, "Nobody gives a fuck if the police does their job, then they can do their job; if not, nobody really cares." So this was more or less.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's apologies for the foul language.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Tarculovski at that time indicate to you what he would do, after you gave him this response?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can you recall if you saw these persons after this particular visit?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Which people? Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Well, you've described to us as having a meeting or having a visit with Mr. Tarculovski, a person named Slavco, a person named Ljube, and another person who you can't recall. And you've described this meeting as occurring on Friday, 10 August 2001. I'm asking you whether or not these same persons came to see you at a time subsequent to 10 August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Mr. Johan Tarculovski also came on Saturday afternoon, late. Mr. Ljube -- pardon, Slavco from the police station in Mirkovci, I have seen him on several occasions; however, as part of the fulfilment of the additional task during the period while I was a commander. And the person whose name I could not remember, I have never seen him again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So you saw Mr. Tarculovski on Saturday afternoon, that would be 11 August 2001. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: But with respect to the person named Ljube and Slavco, were those two people present at the time you saw Mr. Tarculovski on Saturday?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honours, in my previous statement, I said that they might have been present; but now after certain time in discussion with the people from my personal security, which were regular conscripts, I cannot claim, that is, I would rather say that these people were not really present on the 11th of August when Mr. Johan visited me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Just so that we understand. You said that after a certain time in discussion with people from your personal security, did these people in your personal security inform you about whether or not Ljube and Slavco were present? Is that why you've changed your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honour, since I was not sure even then when I gave this statement, I had to, in a certain way, to check whether this claim or statement of mine is correct in order to avoid any misunderstanding and wrong conclusions. And that is why I contacted these people, and they are still my friends. We meet each other, we discuss, we talk. And according to their recollections and what they said, I came to the conclusion that most probably these people were not presented. Because when they, three or four, claimed that Ljube and Slavco was -- were not there on the 11th, this is more believable than my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So the meeting that you had on Saturday, 11 August 2001, with Mr. Tarculovski, was anyone else presented at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: As far as I remember, apart from the dilemma whether Ljube and Slavco were there at the meeting, there was no other person.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could you tell us around what time this meeting was?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I think that it was sometime around -- or after 1700, 1800 hours, at dusk. I could not be more specific than this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell us where this meeting occurred?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: That meeting took place also at the command post, Your Honour, as well as the previous one, where I was at the command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can you recall what happened during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: The purpose of Mr. Johan at that meeting was to check whether I had received the order or not, to receive how far things have advanced. This was my impression, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At that time, did Mr. Tarculovski ask anything of you besides with respect to the receipt of the order?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Nothing more, Your Honour. Just whether I had received the order, whether in the meantime there were any changes or not regarding this issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall what this order was -- what this order pertained to?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Well, then and until recently, I did not know. But after I had given my recent statement with superior officers who were working then at the city command for the city of Skopje, which was the command established then for this purpose, and I was seconded to this command, in 2004, sometime around September or October, they told me that the president of the Republic of Macedonia, as a supreme commander, had issued an order. But I couldn't say anything about the contents of that order because I have never seen it, not until the present day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this conversation that you had with Mr. Tarculovski at that time, was the conversation focused about the same things that you discussed the day before with Mr. Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Only about the order, and let's not repeat from what I stated: How is it possible that someone failed? Where was the interruption in the distribution of that order? And things of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: What was your response to Mr. Tarculovski during this meeting with respect to the order?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honour, my response was always the same. Without an order, without specific tasks given by my superior command, I myself must not undertake any activities --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: -- apart activities pertaining to or tasks or orders to defend the positions of my unit in a case where it is directly attacked.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Now, you mention that you told Mr. Tarculovski that you could not undertake any activities without authority -- without an order from your superiors. What specific activities were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if any action, military, combat action, is planned, in order to act upon the order, then police and their army units are involved; then there must be an order or a decision who will be the commander of that unit, who will participate, who will be the logistics support, how it will be put into action, and all the other issues that are necessary for the -- that are necessary to be resolved.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I think I understand that, but what I'm asking you is: You referenced that you could not undertake any activities. What I'm asking you is: With respect to the conversation you had with Mr. Tarculovski, what activities were you saying you could not undertake, specific activities?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm not understanding what you're trying to ask me. Would you be so kind as to repeat your question. I'm kindly asking you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was probably confusing. I apologise. What I'm asking you is that you say that there were specific activities that you could not undertake specific activities, and you told this to Mr. Tarculovski at that time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And I'm asking you, were these activities related to your battalion and providing any kind of support with respect to what Mr. Tarculovski was asking?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had already mentioned that in the previous meeting with the -- that the representative of the Ministry of the Interior, I was informed that the police is preparing an action to search the grounds because there were information and facts from the field that in the village of Ljuboten a group of terrorists were stationed. And within that planned action of theirs, I could not accommodate them in relation to any issue, any request they would make of me. In this sense, in this context, I tried to explain this to the gentleman, but it was not necessary correct or - I don't know how to say - since he came just to ask me whether I had received the order or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this gentleman you refer to, that would still be Mr. Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I am again unable to understand you. Would you be so kind as to repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I apologise. I was just seeking some clarification. You indicated in your last answer that you tried to explain this to the gentleman, with respect to the fact that you could -- you could not accommodate them in relation to their issues or the requests that they made. I'm asking you who this gentleman is that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: It is now clear to me, Your Honour. The request, or rather, asking for information from me, whether I had received an order or whether I had been given a task by the person who was there on the Friday, the representative of the Ministry of the Interior, the explanations I had given to Mr. Johan were personal. I aimed to clarify the situation for him because he did not ask support or participation of my battalion in this action from me personally, because at that time I was aware that he is within the personal security of the supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At any time during these meetings, did they indicate to you what they wanted you to do as commander of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course. When the units of the Ministry of the Interior and the units of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia are performing a joint combat action, the procedures and standards are well-known, who does what, who supports what. This is agreed and regulated in detail in advance.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Maybe it was my question, but I was asking you what -- if you can recall, what did they want you to do as the commander of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honour, obviously, we can't understand one another. In the meeting on Friday, they only asked -- they only informed me, this gentleman who was the representative of the MOI who introduced himself, that the police is planning to undertake an action in the village of Ljuboten due to reasons that I mentioned before. And they asked me whether I had received an order, whether I had been given a task or any guide-lines from my superior and -- in a case. And I suppose that this was the purpose of their visit. In a case I had received an order or if I was informed about the task, we would then go into details of about my obligations and their obligations. But since I had received no order or task or any guide-lines in relation to this, I then informed them, and the rest of the conversation was simply additional clarification and explanation what needs to be done in such situations; but not regarding the specific actions, but in general, in relation to any action in any field. I don't know whether my clarification is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. I believe that your answer was with respect to Friday. On Saturday, or perhaps even on Friday, did these persons ask for fire support from your battalion?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Mr. Tarculovski, Johan, Your Honour, did not ask. On Saturday he just came again to see whether I had received an order or a task.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please show 65 ter 164, which is tab 10 of today's binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Actually, before we go to this document, Mr. Despodov, I'd like to ask you: On Saturday, what is your response to these particular -- to Mr. Tarculovski's indications on Saturday?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I apologise. I can't understand you. What indications?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You talked about a meeting on Saturday, and you indicated that Mr. Tarculovski asked again about an order. What was your response to Mr. Tarculovski at that time?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I informed him, again, that I still hadn't received any order or a task in relation to any other thing, to any other task, that I had received nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall at that time what his reaction was to you informing him of that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I can tell you his reaction was adequate to my response. He was nervous. He was tense, and maybe it made me even more angry or mad, why something failed. How could there be a disruption in the distribution of orders and tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall if he told you what he would do after you -- after he got the information from you, that you had received no order?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I couldn't remember, Your Honour, what he said and how he said it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. If I could just have a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, if I may ask you -- if I may ask you, could -- would reviewing your statement that you provided during the interview that was conducted July of 2004, would that refresh your memory as to what Mr. Tarculovski told you he was intending on doing?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, Ms. Motoike, what we might do is have our first break now - it's a little early - and you can assist the position during that break, and we will resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, before the recess, I had asked you whether or not reviewing your statement that you had provided to the Office of the Prosecutor in July of 2004 would refresh your recollection as to Mr. Tarculovski's statement and reaction to you after you told him that you did not receive the order. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may look at the statement, then we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please pull up on e-court the transcript of this statement, which is T000-2869-T000-2872. And, specifically, if we could please pull up in the English pages 1 -- page 102; in the Macedonian page 60.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Despodov, I'll read for you, if you could look towards the bottom of the Macedonian version on the page that's being displayed. You're asked -- or actually there's a statement by Thomas Kuehnel. It says: "Yeah, okay. So go on, please, with Saturday. Saturday is the second meeting." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then if we could please turn the page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And drawing your attention to the upper part of this particular page in Macedonian, there's a statement by you, Mr. Despodov, that says in the bottom of the English: "The subject of the discussion was the same as on Friday, and -- but Johan had the main word again. Okay. If I had an order again," and there's something that's indiscernible, "phone calls, not to repeat myself." And then Thomas Kuehnel says: "No. It's just to conjure anything."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could turn the page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: The top says, it's indiscernible, "you need to be precise on that." Then there's a statement by you, Mr. Despodov: "In a nutshell, the demands were the same. Were: Did I receive an order? Am I willing to give them support? Will I participate in the action? He was obviously very nervous why I behaved like that, and he was nervous why the people in the higher -- hierarchy didn't actually accomplish their task or something broken in the chain of command." Then Thomas Kuehnel says: "Okay. And then you say: "When I told him again that there was no chance that me or my units would participate in this action without an order from my superiors, his reaction was pretty angry. He even used obscene language, 'With or without you the police will conducted this operation.' And he swore in the end." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you're referring to the paragraph these words, literally, yes. And I apologise, but I will read it literally, as I said it then: "Well, fuck you, with or without you, the action will take place, and tomorrow or few days afterwards, if a vehicle is blown again, then don't cry," if that is what you were referring at.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And does this refresh your recollection as to what Johan Tarculovski told you in response to you saying you had no order yet?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Essentially, this is it, but I do not interpret this as him saying that he will then implement the action. It is the police. He says: "The action will take place with or without you," but it will be the police who will implement the action, and not him himself. This is how I understood it, and this is the context in which I said it. If I was misunderstood in this, then I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could then move on to a document, Mr. Despodov.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we please - I apologise - show 65 ter 164, which is tab 10 of today's binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Despodov, it might be easier for you to use the hard copy under tab 10 in the binder that's in front of you, because I don't know whether we will be able to manipulate the Macedonian version to display both pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Despodov, this particular document, let me first ask you, in the bottom there in the middle on the right side of the Macedonian version, there's a name, "Kostadinov, Ljupco." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you know who this particular person is, Ljupco Kostadinov?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I know of him, Your Honour. He was assistant to the commander for security in the 1st Guardist Brigade at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recognise the handwriting of this particular document?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I couldn't say whose handwriting it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: May I direct your attention to the left side of the Macedonian version, which is actually the top portion of the English. It says: "I claim that this copy is made from my work notebook of 2001, and it is copied on my presence by the investigator. The notes had been written in the period between 2 August 2001 and 15 August 2001. The information in the notebook is true and no information was added additionally. "I am giving the information from the notebook to the investigator so that he could use it to clear up the events of Ljubotenski Bacila and Ljuboten village in 2001. He cannot use the information for other purposes." And right below that, there's a date, 15 August 2001 [sic]. Do you see the signature there? Do you recognise the signature there as being Ljupco Kostadinov's?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I couldn't say. I don't know what his handwriting looks like.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Well, if we could look at the Macedonian version to the right --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 8 on page 33, I think there is a mistake in the date read out by my colleague. On the document, it says the 15th of August, 2004; and in the transcript, it says 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise. I might have misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could look at the Macedonian version towards -- on the right side. Right below Kostadinov Ljupco, there's also the first-class captain, VP 2993, Skopje; and then it indicates that 2788, 0100 hours, and there's a signature there as well. Do you see that, Mr. Despodov?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please turn to page 13 of the English, which is page 14 of the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you see on the Macedonian version, on the left side, there's a number 27. In the middle, it says 12 August 2001, 1200 hours.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I see it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then in bolder pen marking, there's another -- the same date: "12 August 2001," towards the bottom of the English. And it says: "On Friday evening at 2100 hours, a group of," and it's blank, "persons had come. "They had come to the house of Johan Tarculovski from Kometa, colleagues - 40 for the beginning. "There are 60 to 70 of them in police uniforms. A truck of MVR," which is Ministry of Interior, "had come and had distributed bombs, weapons, and ammunition. They had told to Despodov that they had been ordered to," and it's the next page of the English.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I don't see it. I can't read it in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Towards the bottom on the left side, there is bold pen markings, 12.08.2001, do you see the references made to --

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you see the references that I just made with respect to your name?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I can't really read it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Well, let me read then what the English translation is with respect to this portion. It makes reference to Despodov that: "They had been ordered to overnight in Ljubanci in the rest house and to clean-up Ljuboten from terrorists and bunker." And it goes on to say - and perhaps it's on the right side of the Macedonian - "the President knows that and no one else should know the task. "The Major had approved the accommodation, and they had asked him for an opinion of an expert on how to perform that. "The aim of the task, how much forces he has, manner of action, et cetera. "On Friday, together with them, also Ljube Krstevski, head of PS Butel; commander of PS Mirkovci Slavco and Iliaj - the referent for military matters from Butel. "The inspectors had told them - you have weapons, ammunition, and our logistical support." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting my colleague in her examining, but I would like to object the question asked in this manner because the witness replied that he could not recognise the handwriting. He only knows the name indicated; it is Ljupco Kostadinov. Ljupco Kostadinov as the author of this diary is one of the next witnesses. He would be the one to authenticate this handwriting; and I think that by displaying this document, the memory of this witness is not refreshed because this is not a statement of his.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Apostolski. I think the position is complicated because of the difficulties of displaying the Macedonian original on e-court. It is very difficult to read it. I'm sure that Ms. Motoike will shortly be asking the Macedonian document in the relevant area to be enlarged, to give the witness an opportunity to view what is written more closely, and the witness an opportunity to see whether the English translation assists him to read the Macedonian words. If it does not, well, I agree with you, we would then have reached the end of what could usefully be done at this point with this document. But until that's completed, I think what Ms. Motoike is doing should continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: My last question to you, actually, Mr. Despodov, was with respect to the references made in the right side of the Macedonian version. I read references that were made with respect to the president and approval by the major, and my question to you after reading that passage was: Do you see that on page 28, which is the right side of the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike, can I suggest that if the witness's display is the same as the Bench is receiving, that it would not be possible for him to assist with anything, that we go to display the screen only in Macedonian, and you then ensure that it is enlarged in the right area. And those of us who have hard copies in English can follow the English that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could please -- yes. Thank you. If we could perhaps focus in on the right side of the Macedonian version. I don't know if this can be enlarged any bigger.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, are you able to see now the references that I've read out in English here in the Macedonian version on page 28?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I can see, Your Honour; however, I don't have a comment on this. I couldn't say where this information comes from and how this person reached this information. I will repeat it again, that what we discussed at the meeting, who was there, who was present, both on Friday and Saturday, and I already said that. And Ljupco Kostadinov, I know him just as a person, what position he had, and what he did. This is a statement that I see for the first time. This information within it, I hear them for the first time; and where, from who, and why provided this kind of information to him, I could not really comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Well, can I direct your attention to another paragraph, which is actually on page 29 of the Macedonian -- I'm sorry, page 15 of the Macedonian version. It's on page 14 still of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could, please, focus in only the left side of this particular version in the Macedonian version, enlarging it to the biggest scale possible, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Towards the bottom of this particular page on the left side, if I could just read to you what's indicated, it says: "Johan had said tomorrow at 430 hours, I am starting with the action. The MVR superiors had dissociated themselves. They had asked written document from somebody -- from someone."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've run out of relevant vision on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Ah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We need to see more the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Then it goes on to say: "But Mitre had told him, 'You can start but on your own. I have get an order from above.' But it has been previously agreed to support them." Do you see that, Mr. Despodov, towards the bottom of the page on the left, the paragraph starts with: "Johan ..."

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I can see that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And what I just read to you, does that accord with what you've told us today, and that is you have told them: "You can start on your own, but I have to get an order from above"?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: But the I did not say to -- this to Mr. Johan, but I said it to the gentleman who was there on Friday. And I stand behind this statement, that the police can undertake any type of action, but I can only participate with an order received from my superiors.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: In the very bottom of that page, it says: "Johan," and then it continues to the top of the right side of the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could scroll up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And it goes on to say on this top part: "Johan had gone but M. Mitre had said, 'I do not act without an order,' but they had started." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, again, is that in accord with what you've told us today?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I apologise. In accord with what?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I was confusing. Does that -- is that the same as what you've told us today about what happened?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, Your Honour. Can you be more specific, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is that consistent with what you've told us today with respect to you not acting without an order? Does that statement reflect that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. To him and to my commander, on the 12th, when they came to the location of my battalion, I told them the same, that according to the conversation with the president, he's aware of the action. The action was legally planned. However, whether I did not receive an order, whether it was supposed to be an action together with their army or not, and whether I -- why I did not receive any specific tasks or orders at this particular location, I am not aware even today. And what Ljupco is writing here in his notes, I apologise, but you will have to ask him where this information comes from. And I personally don't understand this other information, what he really wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Are you aware of Ljupco Kostadinov's duties within the battalion or the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: As I already mentioned previously, I know Ljupco Kostadinov. While we were working together, he was assistant commander for security, and his competencies and his scope of work is not known to me, especially the manner and the principle of his work. Where this information comes from and what kind of information it is, I couldn't even guess.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps, at this time, could we please mark this for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Has Exhibit P302, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, if I could show you another document, which is at tab 11 of today's binders, 65 ter 940. The document displayed before you in the Macedonian language, if I could just direct your attention, Mr. Despodov, to the upper left corner of this document. It says: "Republic of Macedonia; Ministry of Defence; ARM," and then it's dated below "12.08.2001, Skopje." It then lists "1st Guard Brigade, Captain 1st class, Ljupco Kostadinov, 12 August 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then in the middle there in bold, it says: "Official Note." And right below that, it says: "Subject: Report on actions and situation in 3rd Guard B, village of Ljuboten, submitted by ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could please turn to page 3 of the English, which is also page 3 of the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At the very bottom of this page in the Macedonian and English versions, do you see, it says: "Assistant to the commander for security, Captain 1st class, Ljupco Kostadinov." Do you see that, Mr. Despodov?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I can see that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could, please, go back to the first page on both documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And directing your attention to the first paragraph in the Macedonian version, towards the middle, it talks about persons who had arrived who were wearing MVR uniforms. It goes on to state: "These persons asked Major Mitre Despodov, who is commander of 3rd Guard B, to provide them with a place to sleep in the mountain lodge in village Ljubanci. Major Despodov asked them on whose orders they had come. They said that this is known to the president and no one else should know about their stay. Major Despodov asked them what their role is here. They answered that they have the task to enter into village Ljuboten and to conduct a search and cleaning of the terrain." Do you see that at the very bottom of the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this paragraph references you as the commander. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: And I was the commander of the 3rd Guardist Battalion. This is something that I repeated several times, Your Honour. This is a fact, the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then it goes on in the second paragraph: "Soon after this conversation, the head of PS," which is police station, "Cair, Ljube Krstevski; the commander of PS Mirkovci, Slavco; and the person Ilija, officer for military issues from PS Cair, arrived at the school in Ljubanci." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I can see that, Your Honour; however, again, I will repeat. They did not arrive one after another. I already said, during this meeting, the representative from the Ministry of Interior, Mr. Johan Tarculovski; Mr. Ljube; and Mr. Slavco came at the same time, and this is the truth. And this information by Mr. Ljupco, I don't know where it comes from and what he wrote in the beginning. At that time, I know that Mr. Johan Tarculovski was part of the security of the president of the state. And what is being mentioned here, the chief from Kometa, 60, 70 people, this is something that I see and hear for the first time. I do apologise. But where this information comes from, you will have to ask him. I personally cannot comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Well, I'm actually asking you about the portion that actually refers to you as commander. And then going on, in the third paragraph, it also mentions you. It says: "The MVR officers contacted Major Mitre Despodov and told him that from them will be the armament and equipment for the above-listed persons, only if he has a need to support the action," we're going over to page 2 of the English, "and for this, he will receive special orders from the president of the state, who will call him by phone." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Something like this was not discussed amongst the two of us. I still stand to what I said earlier, about the meeting, what time it was, and who was present. Other conversations and what is being said here, I will negate it, that I was asked as the commander of the 3rd Guardist Battalion to provide sleeping place. So there is no mountain lodge there. There is just this children's accommodation, and I have never seen 60 or 70 people, nor I heard about that. This is something that I hear for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: With respect to the references that are made in this document as to the arrival of these particular people at the school in Ljubanci, do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: At the school in Ljubanci, no. Such people in this kind of numbers, I have never seen throughout the whole period when I was present there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm just asking -- I'm not talking about the persons referred to in the beginning of the paragraph, Mr. Despodov. If we could just focus our attention on the heads of the police stations that you have already told us about. You indicated that they did arrive, but they all arrived together with Johan. Is that correct? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I do apologise then. I understood it wrong. What I said, this is it, they came together and we were discussing what I mentioned earlier, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And in reference to the task, which is referred to in the bottom of the paragraph 1 in the Macedonian, that last sentence that's -- where you asked them what their role is here, they answered that they had the task to enter into village Ljuboten and to conduct a search and cleaning of the terrain. Was that your information at some point, not from these particular people; but at any time, was that your information that was provided to you?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: In the -- during the phone conversation that I had with the president, he told me that the policemen know what to do, the police, the representative that was sent over, that they know. But the question was whether I received some tasks or orders. I answered that I have not received any orders or tasks. He said that he's going to check this through the general, Sokol Mitrevski, what is where and how, and I will be informed. And since I did not receive any response, I evaluated and I came to the conclusion that the police on its own will organise the action; and from the president, I got certain instructions that I have to undertake measures and activities under my competence. If necessary, I am going to clarify this further, Your Honour, what these measures and activities actually mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Well, actually, I wanted to refer you with respect to the references you made to the president. I wanted to refer you to page 2 of the Macedonian version of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could display that for him, please. It's also page 2 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: The top paragraph on this -- actually, it's the second paragraph, it starts with: "On Saturday, 11 August 2001, the above-listed persons, headed by Johan Tarculovski, conducted reconnaissance in the village of Ljuboten, and in the village they shot at dogs that barked at them. "Around 1700 to 1730 hours, the person, Johan Tarculovski, asked Major Mitre Despodov to shoot at target in the village of Ljuboten, which they previously had determined precisely together with Major Mitre Despodov. Major Despodov did not want to open fire upon the above-mentioned targets without orders, requested approval from the superiors. "Around 1800 to 1900 hours, first the person, Johan, talked with the president of the state, and then Major Despodov personally talked with the president. The president asked him whether he is under the command of General Sokol. Major Despodov answered 'Yes.' The president told him, 'Good. I will talk to General Sokol and I will call you again.'" . Do you recall that event happening?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I remember, and I confirm that this conversation that is mentioned here with the president, as it is stated, is correct; and the rest of it, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Did you ever receive a call from the president after this conversation you reference in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I already mentioned during the meeting, while it lasted on Friday with the people that I already mentioned, Mr. Johan talked to the president; and during a moment while he was talking, he handed the phone to me and he said, "Mr. Despodov, somebody wants to talk to you. The president wants to talk to you." I cannot really recall the wording; however, this was in essence. When I took over the phone, by the voice on the other side of the line, I could recognise the voice of the president. And not to repeat myself, he said what was already mentioned, whether I was really, indeed, the commander; whether I was Mitre Despodov, the commander of the battalion; whether I recognised the voice; whether I'm sure who the person was; et cetera. I have to say that I have met the president on several occasions before that. I was talking to him on the phone because, besides my regular tasks and obligations in the brigade, during the official welcoming parties and sending-off of the president, I had the task of being the cameraman and to document these kind of events at the airport, before the parliament building, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
