utterances.text: I guess what I was asking you is: Was this the only conversation that you had then with the president, which is what you've referenced, when Johan Tarculovski handed you the phone?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: The only conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Macedonian version same page, and English same page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It says: "On Sunday, 12.08.2001, at 0430 hours, the person, Johan Tarculovski, with the other persons," and I believe it says in parenthesis, "(MVR reservists) started the action. Immediately after the start of the action, Captain Nikolce Grozdanovski," which is G-r-o-z-d-a-n-o-v-s-k-i, "called up Major Despodov and informed him about the start of the action, which had been organised by MVR." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall having a conversation with the captain about the start of the action by the MVR?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: A conversation or a report I received from all the superiors at particular location about what they could hear during the night, during the day, they would inform me. But that the action started exactly at 4.30 and it was Johan Tarculovski, about the action, I did not receive information from the subordinates. I only know that the action started around 6.00 a.m., plus or minus 15 minutes. But these shots could be heard earlier. So, personally, to me they did not mean anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Going to the bottom paragraph of the English, if we could scroll down, and if we could scroll down on the Macedonian version because I believe it's towards the bottom. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: The paragraph that starts out, it's the second from the bottom on the Macedonian version, Mr. Despodov, it says: "Around 0800 hours, Major Despodov called the commander and asked him whether he had received any orders from General Sokol Mitrevski for action against the village of Ljuboten. The commander answered that for the present, he had not received any orders; and after this, he called personally General Sokol Mitrevski, who said that he had not issued any orders." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall calling the commander and asking about orders?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honours, in order to clarify, if you allow me to give you more details. Every single morning to my commander, between 6.00, 6.30, I give oral reports about the situation over the night regarding the position of my battalion. That day, on the 12th, around 8.00, give or take 15 minutes, the positions of my unit were attacked with mortar fire, shelling; and for this reason, I called to inform the commander that I will be undertaking appropriate actions according to our military laws and regulations. And, at that time, the shooting in the village have intensified; and on the paces of this more intensive fire in the village, I came to the conclusion, I guess, that the police started the action. As I already said, I don't recall the exact time; however, at 8.00, the positions have been attacked. And as a response to this attack, I ordered that people should start firing. The attack came from the side of Matejce, Kuljm; that is to say, from the side of Skopska Crna Gora. And all the reports I received at that time from my units at those locations were talking about an attack of the positions of my units.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can I just ask you who was your commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Mr. Colonel Kopacev Blazo, as direct superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, did Ljupco Kostadinov come to any of the army positions that day, meaning the 10th or the 11th or 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: On the 12th of August, together with the commander Kopacev Blazo, around half past 11.00, maybe 12.00, when the activities on the position of my units and when my response was already over, but together with Mr. Kopacev and his driver. Before that, on the 11th or 10th, only the 11th, I'm sure he did not come; on the 10th, maybe. I leave some room for a doubt that he might have been there, but maybe in order to find out something more, to get some more information about the mine when my soldiers died, about that incident. For this reason, maybe he was there, but I cannot really claim that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please turn to page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I just wanted to show you one more paragraph, Mr. Despodov, which is actually the bottom of the Macedonian, page 2. And this paragraph, it's the very last paragraph, I believe, of the Macedonian version, Mr. Despodov. It says: "Around 0830 hours, Major Despodov again called the commander who was in the premises of the 1st," Guards Brigade, I assume, "command and asked him whether the superiors know about the action that is being organised and conducted by the MVR in the village of Ljuboten." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall having contact with your commander with respect to this particular action?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I couldn't really confirm this. It is possible. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On what basis?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness is able to at least speak to some of the events, at least with respect to references made by his actions in the particular days in question. He's able to at least recognise that Ljupco Kostadinov -- I'm sorry, Your Honours, maybe I'm addressing the wrong issue. Is it an issue with respect to the content or with respect to the reliability and authenticity of the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the witness, having refreshed his memory - if I can use that term in a rather extended way - has been able to remind -- be reminded of and to tell you about certain events. How do we get to the position of admitting the document from which his memory was refreshed? It's not his document. He's not said he's seen it or approved it or authorised it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's with respect to not only this witness's testimony. He has testified to certain aspects of the document that refer to him and whether or not particular references are true, albeit some of them that he referred to is -- don't jog his memory; but some of it that he does refer to, he indicates, yes, these actions did occur. And with respect to future witnesses that the Prosecution intends on calling, within -- specifically within the battalion, the company battalion, other witnesses will also speak to the contents of the document, and I believe it's relevant in that the information contained also corroborates this witness's testimony as to the events in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for asking the floor, but I wish to object to this document being received because it is written by a person who will be called to testify, and he would be able to authenticate this document. So I think that this is when the Prosecution would be able to seek to tender this written document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber takes the position, Ms. Motoike, that there is no established basis for the admission of this document as evidence. It will, however, be marked for identification. You have the evidence of this witness as to what his memory is related to the events in this document. If it proves to be the case that other witnesses are able to confirm some of the passages, the position may change. But you will be aware that it's basically the evidence of the witness from -- and each witness from their recollection of events that will be material, and so far you have not been able to impress us that this whole document will ever be a document that will be admissible. When we come to the actual author, if we do, it may present a different picture, as Mr. Apostolski has indicated. So it will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P303, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please display another document for Mr. Despodov, which is 65 ter 213. It is at tab 12 of today's binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, looking at this particular document, in Macedonian version, if I could just draw your attention to the upper left corner. It appears to be a stamp, and then it says: "Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Defence, General Staff, 1st Guardist Brigade." And then it also says: "Addressed to Major-General Sokol Mitrevski," and then above that is a date within the stamp, "12 August 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I see it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recognise that seal as one coming -- the stamp as one coming from the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: That is the seal of the Guardist Brigade within which I was working.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention to the -- actually, it says -- towards the bottom of the English, which is paragraph 3, paragraph 3 of the Macedonian, it references a time. It says: "Between 1730 and 1800 on 11 August 2001, Johan Tarculovski engaged some of the houses by fire of 64-millimetre grenade-launchers, 'Zolja.' He then requested Major Mitre Despodov to support him with 120-millimetre mortar fire, which the latter declined." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I see it, Your Honour. I see that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall having a conversation with Johan Tarculovski about support for 120-millimetre mortar fire?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: The allegations or the data presented in this quote do not correspond to a conversation that Johan and I actually had, Your Honour. I stated already what Johan and I discussed on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could we turn to page 3 of this document, which is also page 3 of the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can I ask you, Mr. Despodov, if you could look at the bottom of this document, it indicates "Blazo Kopacev, Commander Colonel." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I see it. Commander Colonel Blazo Kopacev, his signature there, but I could not guarantee whether the signature is his or not. I cannot comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Does it look like the signature of Colonel Kopacev?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: It is a signature, but I haven't seen his signature since 2001, so I could not really remember whether this signature is his or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 1 again of the document in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And drawing your attention to the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could scroll down on the Macedonian version, which is the last paragraph of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Despodov, there is a reference to this call from the president, if I could just read for you the paragraph. "Between 1800 and 1900 on 11 August 2001, Johan Tarculovski personally called the President from the command post of the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Guardist Brigade; and after a brief discussion, the president requested that Major Mitre Despodov speak to him in person. (As the commander showed up), the President asked him: 'If you are under the command of General Sokol?' The latter said: "'Yes.' And the President told him: 'Good. I will speak to General Sokol and will call you back.'" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 in the English, staying on page 1 of the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: The top part of page 2, the bottom part of page 1 in the Macedonian, it says: "After 2200 hours on the same day, the above-mentioned persons from the Ministry of the Interior, led by Johan Tarculovski, came for the second time to Mitre Despodov regarding the action. Johan Tarculovski told all of them that the action starts at 4.30 a.m., regardless whether or not there would be armed support. Major Despodov, Mitre, told that he has no authority to support the action. But despite that, Major Despodov undertook all measures in order to implement the action successfully in case it was approved by our side." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I see it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is that an accurate reflection of what your -- what happened that day at that time?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And what part is inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: The time of the meeting, I will repeat it once again. On Saturday, the 11th, Johan and I had a conversation about the issues that I've mentioned already. Where did this data come from, these things alleged in his information, I do not know. If I remember correctly, I did not tell the commander the things written here precisely, that on the Friday, Saturday from the brigade command police check-points, reconnaissance patrols, and the other bodies that were working on collecting data about the deployment and the activities of the terrorist groups in that region received a warning that I should be ready, and I should take measures to increase the security as well as the alertness of my units. And, in this context, I informed him that I had taken measures, not measures as indicated here. Why is his comment as it is, you will need to ask the author of the report. I really regret that it is so, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So you're -- one of the points of clarification is that the action that's referred to, you say -- it says here last sentence: "But despite that, Major Despodov undertook all measures in order to implement the action successfully in case it was approved by our side." If I'm understanding you correctly, you mean to say that you did not undertake any actions to implement this action that was referred to by Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I, as a battalion commander - I said this already - I received information that there were terrorists -- serious threats, that my units, my positions, would be attacked by the terrorist groups. If I remember correctly, Xhavit Hasani was the commander of that unit there. And I was literally told, especially by the defence of the city of Skopje command - and I have indicated this in my previous statement - that he had threatened to -- to raise or -- the ground. And with no particular reference to the people I was working with, they did not have any particular information about the subject matter of your question. And it was in this context and towards this aim that I undertook measures, and not in support to the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we mark this for identification, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P304, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: As commander of the 3rd Guardist Battalion, did your battalion also keep a diary with respect to events that had occurred in your battalion -- your battalion's area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was supposed to be kept, but this task was not completed with sufficient quality.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if I could show you 65 ter 652, please, which is tab 5 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we please turn the Macedonian version clock-wise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, looking at the documented before you - if we could, thank you, scroll to the right - in the Macedonian version, there is -- under the coat of arms, there are words that say: "Ministry of Defence, General Staff of ARM," and then below that it says: "Military diary of the 3rd Guardist Battalion." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Does this look like one of the diaries that you kept as part of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: This is my personal handwriting. I have written this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 3 of the English, which is page 2 of the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Despodov, if I could draw your attention --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could - thank you - enlarge the right side of the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, can you see the handwriting on that screen?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I see it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is -- do you recognise the handwriting that's displayed there?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: In the right-hand column, the penultimate right-hand column, at the beginning at the top, I think it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And referring to the top, it says -- there are columns there, and it says: "Date, contents, source, and remarks." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes. In the column source, there, Your Honour, that part of the handwriting is mine, my personal handwriting. While in the column content, I could not recognise the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then looking at the date, it says, "10 August," it refers to. And just briefly looking at the contents, so we can get some perspective on the year for this diary, it says: "In the area of Basinec, at about 0745 hours, a vehicle of the 2nd Company had hit two explosive devices planted by terrorists in ambush, while bringing soldiers on a regular shift at the check-point." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, again, just so that we get a context of the year of this particular diary, would that be in 2001?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Precisely on the date, 10th of August, 2001, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could turn the page, which would be page 2 in the Macedonian and page 4 in the English, and if we could enlarge the Macedonian version, the left side. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, again, there are columns on this page. And as you go down the date column, it appears to be in chronological order starting with 12 August and then ending with 13 August. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, again, does this page contain any of your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: The words at the bottom, the date, "13th of August, 2001," that is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could draw your attention to the first entry on this particular page, "12 August," it says in the contents column: "At the period of time between 11.00 till 1700 hours, during the," and I believe there's a portion that's illegible ineligible for translation, "of the ministers of the MVR," Ministry of Interior, "in Ljuboten village, the terrorists were firing from," and there's another illegible portion, "and Jecmeniste," I apologise for my mispronunciation "towards our positions with 82-millimetre mortars. "At the area of the company, 12 mortar shells had fallen. We fired back with 120-millimetre mortars and 76-millimetre cannon towards the positions of the terrorists." And then to the right, it says the source is the commander of the 2nd company. Would this be Mario Jurisic, who you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, company commander Mario Jurisic. But what is written here is something that I see for the first time or maybe I don't understand it well. But the time is inaccurate, 1100 to 1700 hours, that time until 1700 on the 12th of August. I am not clear about this. I don't remember, and I don't understand what he wanted to say with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P305, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we next move on to another document that I could show, 65 ter 229, which is tab 9 of today's binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Despodov, if I could just ask you first: Mario Jurisic was under your command, is that right, as part of the company?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this particular document, the handwriting, in Macedonian that's displayed before you?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I recognise the document. I was shown it at the interview before, and it bears my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. The handwriting, with respect to this document, though, is this the handwriting of Mario Jurisic?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I suppose so. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of the Macedonian, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At the very bottom, there's a signature. Do you recognise the signature there?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I couldn't affirm with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: The translation says -- it says: "Commander of VB, military unit, 2454," and it's signed by Lieutenant Jurisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could go to the first page, please, of the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At the very top of this document, it's handwritten, it says: "Report." And then it says: "In relation to the military activities on the 12th August 2001." It goes on to say: "At 0800 hours, on the 12th August 2001, one could hear shots in the area of Ljuboten village. The right wing of defence of the company had informed me from the observation post 'Smok' that they came under attack by machine-gun and sniper fire. I immediately informed the commander of the battalion, who ordered me and my deputy to climb up to the position and perceive the situation." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the commander that Mario Jurisic is referring to, is that you?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then in the bottom of page 1, in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could scroll down a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It says: "From the old house under the mosque, with a sniper, and from the last new houses close to the road, a machine-gun fire has been opened against our positions."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then page 2 of the Macedonian if we could go there, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It goes on to say, after a sentence: "After the activation of the cannons, DTG, terrorist groups, started to move in the front part of the village and at the same time continued to shoot at our positions. I immediately requested an approval from the commander of the battalion to use 82-millimetre mortars; and after an approval, I fired five projectiles of 82-millimetres against the DTG, terrorist groups, on the front parts of the houses. The police had already entered the village, so we stopped the activities." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then at the very bottom of the Macedonian version, bottom of the English, it says: "Further on, our activities against Ljuboten village had stopped. The police are undertaking the further activities." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So is it correct to say that the army then, at some point, stopped their involvement, and it was the police that entered the village?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Did the army ever enter Ljuboten village that day?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall the events described that I've told you about, with respect to this document, do you recall those events happening on 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I apologise. Do you mean the events from this statement by Mr. Jurisic? I completely, fully, recall they happened as they are described here, with the exception of his remark at the very end. Further, our activities in relation to the village of Ljuboten stopped. I believe that he's talking about the locations that were firing at our units. When this kind of activity stopped, then I ordered for the response to be ended as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Because to my subordinates I was ordering, when I would receive a report from them that a certain location has been attacked, they should respond and they should be firing only in such case upon my order. And if they cannot get me on line in order for me to approve it, then they should exercise their assessment. Depending on the threats to the position, to the men, then they can act independently on their own. These are our rules, procedures.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this be tendered, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On what basis, Ms. Motoike?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Again, Your Honours, this report speaks to the military activities by the Republic of Macedonia Army on that day, and I have to indicate, again, to the Chamber that there will be another witness who will speak to the particular activities. And this report indicates the reporting system with respect to the Macedonian Army and the fact that these events did happen corroborates the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will not be admitted, Ms. Motoike. If you want it marked for identification, it can be.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P306, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, I'd like to show you another diary, which is 65 ter 670, and it's at tab 6 of today's binder. And my question to you, first, is: Did the 1st Guardist Brigade also keep a diary with respect to events that had occurred in the area of the brigade's responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And looking at this particular document, the right side of the Macedonian version, it's written in -- it's handwritten. Does this look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I think that, during the previous interview, this was a document that was shown to me. If this is the same document, then it is familiar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if I could just draw your attention to the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Actually, the translation does not correspond. Perhaps -- my apologies to the Chamber and all the parties. I believe that the exhibit has the Macedonian version attached to the actual English version. So with the assistance of the usher, maybe we could display the translation and the original Macedonian version via the ELMO. It is tab 6. And to assist you would need the hard copy of page 1 and the hard copy of page 5. Page 5 of the Macedonian actually bears the ERN N001-4722. I believe that Mr. Despodov might have it in his hands.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, could you hand that to the usher to display. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I don't suppose there's any way of making this a little bit darker. I assume it's displaying it exactly as it's depicted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is very difficult for me to read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Despodov, I could get you another hard copy to have in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that would help. Would it assist if we had the second break now, Ms. Motoike?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours, it would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will do that, and we resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, with respect to this particular document, actually, the Prosecutor at this time will not inquire of this witness with respect to this document. So I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Motoike. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. Could we kindly ask the usher to lower the ELMO so that I can see the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Despodov.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague, Mr. Mettraux, I represent Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Before I start putting questions to you, I am going to caution you about something, or rather, kindly request you to do something. I understand the language that you speak, and I assume that you understand the language that I speak. Therefore, you could answer every one of my questions very rapidly, without waiting for the interpretation. However, both my question and your answer have to be interpreted so that the Honourable Trial Chamber and our colleagues in this courtroom would know what it is that you are testifying about. Therefore, I kindly ask you to pause slightly for the interpretation of my question to finish, and then provide your answer. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Very well, Mrs. Edina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I understood the answers you gave my colleague correctly, my colleague the Prosecutor, practically you are a professional military man. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Up to 1st of October, 2005, I was a professional military official; and from 1st of October, 2005, I am a civil servant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You graduated from the military academy in Belgrade in 1982. Is that correct? 1982, right?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After that, you went to serve in the Yugoslav People's Army in Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Not in Sarajevo, but in Visoko. In Sarajevo, I came to service in 1987.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, since Visoko is a small town, not far away from Sarajevo, at that time, you were serving in Bosnia-Herzegovina; that is to say, in the broader area of the town of Sarajevo, that is to say, the small town of Visoko and metropolitan Sarajevo. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 1989, you were transferred to Kosovo from Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you remained in Kosovo until 1991. Is this information correct, that information that we have available here?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Due to what happened in the former SFRY, you left the Yugoslav People's Army in 1991, and you returned to the Republic of Macedonia that you come from originally; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, for one year, you were not professionally engaged in the army; rather, you had a business of your own. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Not the whole year, but since November 2001 -- pardon, sorry, 1991 until April 1992. So this is more or less six or seven months.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, as you've already said to my learned friend, in April 1992, you were engaged yet again, but this time in the Army of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Despodov, that after the independence of the Republic of Macedonia was declared, in the republic, various reforms were carried out. Therefore, there were certain reforms in the armed forces of the Republic of Macedonia, too?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you started working in the Army of the Republic of Macedonia, for the most part, you were engaged in work in the staff of the brigade, but most -- most of all in training?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, in the spring of 2001, you were transferred from the centre for training to a commander -- to become commander of a tactical unit in Tetovo. Is that information correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This order regarding your transfer and your new appointment is one that you received verbally from your superior officer. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In mid-June 2001, you were appointed commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Guards Brigade that was deployed in the area of -- the area that is north of Skopje, notably the area of Skopska Crna Gora. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before you were appointed battalion commander, you personally did not have any true combat experience. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The same could be said of the soldiers who, for the most part, made up your battalion; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although you are a professional soldier, as a member of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia, you did not have any special training for a certain type of combat against terrorist and sabotage groups that would carry out incursions in the territory of the Republic of Macedonia; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to put it to you, Mr. Despodov, that not only for ordinary people but also for you soldiers, it was quite unexpected that after -- the Republic of Macedonia in 1999 made a maximum effort to help the people of Kosovo who were seeking shelter in Macedonia at the time of the NATO strikes. So after all these efforts, it was a big surprise to you that now in the territory of Macedonia such terrorist and sabotage attacks were taking place?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you are a professional soldier, I shall take the liberty of putting a few brief questions to you in relation to the establishment of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia and the chain of command in the units that you served in. You said that there were certain reforms; however, the basic principles pertaining to the work in command in a modern army were retained in the Macedonian Army, too. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although I do not have any military training, nevertheless, I would like to ask you whether it is correct that these basic principles, upon which the Army of the Republic of Macedonia were based, were the principles of unity of command, when using troops and resources; then singleness of command; and also the duty and obligation to carry out orders issued by superior officers, because these are basic principles and the Army of the Republic of Macedonia functioned on that basis, too. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The decisions that a subordinate person had to carry out, as well as the orders of superior officers, could have been issued both in writing and verbally. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And precisely, a few moments ago, you gave an answer to one of my questions; namely, that your transfer to the unit until Tetovo was carried out on the basis of an oral order. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, as a soldier, you probably know, and I believe that in this way I am going to end this brief recollection of how the Army of the Republic of Macedonia works, you know that a subordinate can refuse to carry out the order issued by a superior officer only if its implementation would constitute a crime. Is that one of the principles upon which the Army of Macedonia is based?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to put it to you that not a single other state organ in the Republic of Macedonia is not organised on the basis of such principles, but that it is only the Army of the Republic of Macedonia that is, you will agree with me, won't you, that these are the principles of the organisation of the army, not of other state organs?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to questions put by my learned friend, you referred to your conversation with the president of the Republic of Macedonia. Tell me, is it correct that in accordance with the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia - perhaps you know the exact article. If I were to jog your memory, it is Article 79 of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia - the President of the Republic of Macedonia is the Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: I don't recall the article; however, I know the content, that he is the Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces in the republic, a chief commander of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the armed forces of the Republic of Macedonia are primarily made up of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia, while there are other laws, like the Law on Defence, specify when it is that the police is part of the armed forces, too. Do you know that from your own work in the Army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to these duties, as you mentioned your conversation with the president of the republic, you certainly know that the president of the republic within his own authority has the power to order mobilisation, to order the use of the army, to establish the mode of command, and to make other decisions and orders, as envisaged by the Law on Defence and other laws of the Republic of Macedonia. Are these some of his duties?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you said a few moments ago, in certain situations, the police also becomes an integral part of the armed forces. And if I were to put it to you that in actual fact the president of the republic, in accordance with the Law on Defence, is authorised to order the use of the police for carrying out combat tasks in war, then you can agree with me that that is his right and responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Likewise, if I were to put it to you that according to the Law on Defence of the Republic of Macedonia, it is established that police units can be used for carrying out combat tasks, but only as an integral part of the army, then you can agree with me, can you not, that when there are joint operations involved, the police is within and under the command of the army. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although you spoke very briefly about the situation in the area where your battalion was deployed, I would like to ask you to tell me a bit more about the situation there in 2001. Can you agree with me that, in 2001, the situation in the Republic of Macedonia was rather undefined because the parliament had not declared a state of war?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, although a state of war had not been declared, public law and order and the security of the country, in particular in the northern, north-western parts of the country, was significantly endangered due to the numerous terrorist attacks in those areas. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, can we say that these attacks actually endangered the vital functions of the state in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can we say, Mr. Despodov, that those were the reasons why from March 2001, the Army of the Republic of Macedonia also took part in eliminating the terrorist and sabotage groups?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as I continue putting questions to the witness, I would like to use some other documents, and we have, therefore, prepared binders for the Trial Chamber, for our colleagues of the Prosecution, and for the witness himself. I would now like to ask that the witness be shown 1D-49.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Despodov, I would like to ask you to look at the document that is after tab 1. This is a decision, as you can see in the upper left-hand corner, issued by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, dated the 5th of March, 2001. It pertains to the use of the units of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia. Do you see that it is the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski, that signed this document?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at the text of this decision a bit. It is under seal. And could you please look at paragraph 1 of this decision, and then I would like to put a question to you. In paragraph 1, does this decision not confirm your own knowledge and the answers that you have just given me; namely, that already in March, the Army of the Republic of Macedonia was engaged in eliminating sabotage terrorist groups?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Please, can you repeat the question. I did not understand it well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these documents are otherwise under seal, so I would not like to have them disclosed to the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Despodov, is whether it is correct that by this decision the president establishes that units of the Army of Macedonia should respond to attacks and provocations by diversion terrorist groups against the units of the army?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The content of this decision corresponds to your own knowledge and experience from that time because you, as a soldier, at that time also knew that the army responded to diversion and terrorist attacks by Albanian groups?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you to have a look at the document under tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 65 ter number is 641. The Macedonian version is N00 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] N002648 [as interpreted] -- [In English] 6048. [Interpretation] N002648-ET is the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, yet again, you see a decision of the Commander-in-Chief; that is to say, the president of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the upper left-hand corner, you can see that it is dated the 19th of March, 2001, and it pertains to the use of the army for carrying out operations.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This decision was signed by the president of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the text of the decision, you will see that this decision also pertains to carrying out operations aimed at destroying terrorists, this time in the area of Tetovo. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that this decision taken by the president is actually the exercise of his rights and responsibilities as Commander-in-Chief, giving him the power to make a decision on using the army. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this be admitted as a Defence document, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As 1D-79, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, now I would like to ask you to take a look at the document under tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the 65 ter number is 643. The Macedonian reference is N026055, and the English version is N002-6055-ET.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is also a document of the president of the Republic of Macedonia, dated the 28th of March, 2001. You can see that on the basis of what it says in the upper left-hand corner, too. It also pertains to the use of the army for carrying out certain operations. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Again, it is signed by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The content of this decision, namely, paragraph 1, shows - and I hope that you can agree with me on this - that, yet again, the president of the Republic of Macedonia is exercising his rights and responsibilities as Commander-in-Chief, establishing what the duties are of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia, and the territory where these tasks would be carried out. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask that this document also be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D-80, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While answering my previous questions, you said that a superior officer can issue an order in writing and orally. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The president, as the Commander-in-Chief of the army, can issue an order, both in writing and orally. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to look at a document -- the document under tab 2, 1D -- sorry, sorry. It is Exhibit 1D-51.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is one page in Macedonian and one page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the upper left-hand corner, you can see that this is a document of the president of the Republic of Macedonia, his office, that the date of the document is the 18th of March, 2001, and that it constitutes a record of the meeting between the president of the Republic of Macedonia and the Chief of General Staff of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, in the middle of paragraph 2, you can see that what is stated is that after the situation was discussed in the area of Tetovo that: "President Trajkovski issued an oral order to the Chief of General Staff to do whatever is possible quickly, efficiently, and" -- that is to say: "Urgent, efficient, and decisive offensive action in collaboration with MUP forces for the neutralisation of the terrorist groups in the region of Tetovo." Can you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My first question, Mr. Despodov, is: This particular part of the record that was compiled, and it was compiled by Nikola Dimitrov, national security advisor to the president of the Republic of Macedonia. I beg your pardon. So is it correct that this portion that we read out now confirms that President Trajkovski, like the other superior personnel in the Republic of Macedonia, issued and could issue orders orally as well?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that from the second part of this record, we can see that the president is ordering coordination with the forces of the Ministry of the Interior; and, in this way, he is expressing his rights and responsibilities vis-a-vis the police of the Republic of Macedonia, too?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This document has already been admitted into evidence. A few more questions that are perhaps of relevance in relation to the position of your battalion in 2001 in the area of Skopska Crna Gora. Tell me, Mr. Despodov, is it correct that one of the basic tasks of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia is to guard the borders of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in peacetime, the border belt that is controlled by the Army of the Republic of Macedonia extends ten kilometres from the border of the respective neighbouring states?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because of terrorist actions and incursion by terrorist groups in the territory of the Republic of Macedonia, is it correct that in 2001 a decision was that the border belt should be extended so as to include 20 kilometres, and that that area would be under the control of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia as well?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A few moments ago, we said that the situation in that period of time in the Republic of Macedonia was rather undefined, because a state of war had not been declared; and, in some parts of the country, the security situation was so threatened that it endangered the security of the entire country. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the same time, that was the reason why the president of the Republic of Macedonia ordered partial mobilisation of the army in the Republic of Macedonia. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In actual fact, let us just repeat this, the Army of the Republic of Macedonia is a standing army, on the one hand, but it also has its reservists; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The reserve force consists of citizens of the Republic of Macedonia who are of age and who had completed their military service beforehand?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to the decision taken by the Commander-in-Chief, the reserve force is mobilised either partially or there is general mobilisation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, in the Republic of Macedonia, there was only partial mobilisation; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, in your own battalion, you had a significant number of reservists; right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Maybe 95 per cent. Only the superiors were from the regular composition of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to the regulations of the Republic of Macedonia, the reserve force had to be changed every month. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For you, the commanders, that was a significant problem because, first of all, you had to train the reservists who had been called-up to familiarise them with the area, carry out training in terms of the use of weapons, and other forms of training that would turn them into a disciplined army structure, as required. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, and this was a major problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, if I were to remind you now, in mid-July, the General Staff in response to this lack of discipline among the reserve force indicated special tasks aimed at a much better training of reservists than had been the case until then. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I would like to ask you to look at the document under tab 5. There is one more decision here. This is Exhibit 1D-50. And as you can see, Mr. Despodov, from the upper left-hand corner, yet again, this is a decision made by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, and it is signed by the president, Boris Trajkovski -- or actually, it is somebody else who signed on behalf of the president, Boris Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision dated the 3rd of May, 2001. If you look at the first paragraph of this decision, yet again, it talks about the coordinated action between the army units and the units of the Ministry of the Interior, in carrying out operations in the areas of Vaksince and Slupcane. And in paragraph 2, it says that it is a decision of the Chief of General Staff of the army that will regulate this decision. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov, yet again, is this proof that already in the month of May the president of the republic, as the Commander-in-Chief, is drawing on his own authority vis-a-vis the Ministry of the Interior, and at the same time establishing that command and decisions in that operation are in the hands of the army commands?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please look at the document under tab 6. That is Exhibit 1D-58, dated the 14th [as interpeted] of June, 2004. And as you can see, yet again, this is a decision of the president of the Republic of Macedonia, who also signed this decision.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Just a moment, I can't --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is right after 6. You have tab 6, and it's the first document right after that.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Dated 4th of June, you said?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And in item 1 of the decision, you have, again, a decision about the use of army units and the units of the Ministry of the Interior, which would fall under the authority of the president as the Commander-in-Chief, as you testified a while ago. Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, in paragraph 3, it is, again, established as the Law on Defence provides and the Law on Army of the Republic of Macedonia provides that the commander of the operation will be a given officer from the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this decision, as you as a military officer know and as is your practice, is in conformity with the decisions of the president of the Republic of Macedonia and the authority he established during the crisis in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Answering the questions of my learned colleague, you testified that you needed to receive a given order to use force and that your subordinate officers, company commanders, could also receive one. But you also stated that if they could not contact you through the communications system, that they would need to make their own assessment of the situation and decide about the specific situation on the field. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document under tab 34 -- I apologise. No, tab 7. I apologise. That is Exhibit 1D-52.

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dated 7th of August, 2001. And before I ask you something in relation to this document, I will remind you of the answer you gave to my learned colleague, when you stated that after these events in 2001, when you were transferred to a post in the city command, you learned that the president had made a certain decision about the actions or the conduct of the army in a given situation. If I understood you well, you never saw that decision, and particularly you were not aware of it in August 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This decision is actually dated the 7th of August, 2001. Also, it is, again, signed by Boris Trajkovski, the President of the Republic of Macedonia. And it actually denotes the right to self-defence and the right of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia to return fire against those who are attacking the army positions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is what you testified about before this Court, that you yourself would issue an order to return fire at the moment when your positions were under threat. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the item 1, in paragraph 2, it is stated: "I underline that the measure taken by the army also includes instances when the members of the Ministry of Interior are in danger from the attacks." I think you will agree with me that the president, as a supreme commander, has an authority to issue such order to the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you discussed -- when you spoke to the president on the 10th or the 11th of August, when was it that you spoke to the president? Could you remind me?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: It was the 10th, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when he, as far as I understood, asked you whether you had the decision, and when you see now this decision, can you tell me, was the president referring to a decision that he had issued previously, in writing, to the army units?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that if you were aware of this decision, then a question would not be asked whether you needed to protect the units and ring the village in case they were attacked. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITRE DESPODOV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this might be a convenient time to -- for me to finish this part of the cross-examination. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. We adjourn now, resuming tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of June, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
